title: Text-to-Speech Pipeline
interviewAnswer: Modern TTS maps text/phonetic representations to acoustic features or latent speech and then uses a vocoder/decoder to synthesize waveform audio. Quality involves intelligibility, naturalness, speaker/style control and latency.
keyPoints: Acoustic model and vocoder are distinct conceptual stages.
Evaluate with human listening plus objective diagnostics.
why: Text-to-Speech Pipeline is a recurring foundation across data science and machine learning because it affects both theoretical correctness and practical system behavior.
deepDive: Modern TTS maps text/phonetic representations to acoustic features or latent speech and then uses a vocoder/decoder to synthesize waveform audio. Quality involves intelligibility, naturalness, speaker/style control and latency. Acoustic model and vocoder are distinct conceptual stages. Evaluate with human listening plus objective diagnostics. The interview-level skill is not merely recalling the definition: explain the assumptions, what diagnostic evidence you would inspect, and what alternative you would choose when those assumptions fail.
workedExample: Generate spoken navigation instructions while preserving names/numbers with appropriate text normalization.
commonMistakes: Using the concept mechanically without checking assumptions or data semantics.
Reporting one metric/result without examining uncertainty, slices or failure modes.
followUps: What assumptions or limitations does Text-to-Speech Pipeline have?

production: In production, make assumptions explicit, validate on representative slices, compare with a simple baseline and monitor the signals that can drift.
